summary: This article explains how Earth is divided into climate zones such as tropical, temperate, polar, and desert, based mainly on latitude but also on altitude and dry descending air, why Saudi Arabia sits in a desert zone, and how climate shapes where and how people live.
introduce: Show the title “Climate Zones Around the World” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: how far north or south a place is from the equator
having mild weather with four different seasons
hot and often rainy, found near the equator

challengeTerms.def: one half of the Earth, usually divided by the equator
water that falls from the sky as rain, snow, or hail
the height of land above sea level

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that where a place sits on Earth decides almost everything about how people live there? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how latitude shapes Earth's climate zones, and explain why Saudi Arabia is in a desert, arid zone even though that depends on more than latitude alone.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review latitude, temperate, and tropical, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses hemisphere, precipitation, and elevation to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
